name: limit_copy_that_never_existed
why: THE REASON `suppress_instance` CHECKS. A pattern builds only the copies that fit in the material and answers «succeeded» just the same -- it is note 80y, and it is still true. Asking to remove a copy that never existed SUCCEEDS: `ModifyDefinition` answers true, the array is written, and nothing changes in the part. Whoever reads the answer believes they removed a hole that was not there.
_why_the_NINTH_is_asked: Here the row fits entirely: four holes, three copies. We ask to remove copy 9, which does not exist -- and it is the WORKABLE way to build this red. The road that would come to mind -- a row that sticks out of the part, so that the fourth copy is not born -- cannot be taken from the catalogue: `linear_pattern` counts the copies made and refuses by itself. Tried: starting from -60 with pitch 40 it answers «I counted 1 of the 3 requested» and the pattern is not born. Which is good news about the product and bad news about how to write this case.
_why_the_check_is_still_needed: Because a pattern can come from outside: made by hand in SOLIDWORKS before the plan begins, or by a future operation that does not count the copies. The guardian of `suppress_instance` does not lean on that of `linear_pattern`: it looks at the part.

expect.tolerance_why: the centre is read from CylinderParams

message_includes: put the pattern back as it was

expect.why: AFTER THE REFUSAL THE ARRAY WENT BACK TO EMPTY. If the refused step had left the 9 in, here we would read [2, 9] -- that is a refusal that changed the part anyway, which is the worse of the two.

expect.tolerance_why: the three remaining centres, read from CylinderParams
expect.why: and the same operation, on a copy that EXISTS, works: without this line the refusal above would not tell a check that works from one that refuses everything
